newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks retreat after posting early gains.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks retreat after posting early gains.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks gave back all of their gains Monday as investors cashed their profits from a rally that was seen as a typical end-of-month surge.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 1.49 points at 6,005.53 after gaining more than 35 points earlier. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 13-8 on moderate volume of 219 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 0.42 of a point at 1,222.18, and the American Stock Exchange index was down 0.61 at 569.18.

"The strongest part of any month are the last few days of the old month and the first few days of the new one," said Harry Laubscher, an analyst at Tucker Anthony. "We were anticipating a rally at this point."
Analysts said the initial upturn was driven by strength in energy stocks, which rose on the back of further increases in crude oil prices.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, oil was up 47 cents at a five-year high of $25.33 a barrel.
Exxon Corp. was up 1 at 89-1/2 and Texaco Inc. shaved some of its gains and was up 3/8 at 103-5/8.

Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. said with the third quarter earnings period effectively over, investors were now focused on the economy and the slew of data due out this week, including the October jobs report due on Friday.
"The market is shifting its attention to the economy and interest rates, a combination that will dominate this week," he said.

"The data will be fast and furious this week. It will be a crucial week which will determine the direction of interest rates, stock prices and you can bet it will influence the Federal Reserve when the FOMC (the Fed's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee) meets on Nov. 13."
He said the market was likely to keep marking time in anticipation of the data.

Among special situations, Loctite Corp. surged 26 percent after Henkel KGaA of Germany said it intended to acquire for $56 per share the 65 percent of Loctite it does not already own. Loctite soared 11-3/8 to 57-3/8.

Physician Reliance was the most actively traded Nasdaq stock, falling 4-5/16 to 5-3/16 after reporting third quarter earnings and warning that its fourth quarter results would be similar to those in the third quarter.
